genesis.30.p1.b1.text: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister.

genesis.30.p1.b2.text: “Give me children, or I will die!”

genesis.30.p1.b3.text: “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”

genesis.30.p1.b4.text: “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”

genesis.30.p2.b1.text: and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.

genesis.30.p2.b2.text: “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.”

genesis.30.p2.b3.text: “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.”

genesis.30.p3.b1.text: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.

genesis.30.p3.b3.text: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,

genesis.30.p3.b4.text: “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.”

genesis.30.p4.b1.text: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother,

genesis.30.p4.b2.text: “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

genesis.30.p4.b3.text: “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?”

genesis.30.p4.b4.text: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him

genesis.30.p5.b1.text: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.

genesis.30.p5.b2.text: “God has given me a good gift,” … “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.”

genesis.30.p5.b3.text: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.

genesis.30.p6.b1.text: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,

genesis.30.p6.b3.text: “May the LORD add to me another son.”

genesis.30.p7.b1.text: “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.

genesis.30.p7.b2.text: “If I have found favor in your eyes, … the LORD has blessed me because of you.”

genesis.30.p7.b3.text: “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”

genesis.30.p7.b4.text: The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”

genesis.30.p8.b2.text: “You do not need to give me anything,” … So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future.

genesis.30.p8.b3.text: “Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”

genesis.30.p8.b4.text: That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats … and he placed them under the care of his sons. Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob,

genesis.30.p9.b1.text: Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.

genesis.30.p9.b2.text: … And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.

genesis.30.p9.b3.text: So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.

genesis.30.p9.b4.text: Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.
